correctness.rationale: Exhausted Ω(n)<=3 factorization shapes. Prime powers p^2,p^3 have a=1+p and cannot divide; pq with p<q requires p+1=q, forcing 6. For p²q, the two complementary divisors q and p² straddle sqrt(n), so a=1+p+min(q,p²). For q>p², coprimality gives prime q=p²+p+1; for q<p², a=p+q+1>p,q must equal p² (giving q=p²-p-1) or pq (giving (p-1)(q-1)=2, thus 12 and 18). For distinct p<q<r, the small divisors are exactly 1,p,q,min(r,pq); case r>pq yields (p+1)(q+1) contradicting every feasible prime divisor, while r<pq gives a=p+q+r+1 and parity/order contradictions for a in {pq,pr,qr}. No squarefree triple works. Each converse checked by small-divisor formula. Independent integer-arithmetic classification for every 2<=n<60,000 with Ω(n)<=3 matched the theorem. No assertion concerning polynomial prime infinitude.

value.rationale: The small-divisor sum is a natural arithmetic function studied analytically; exact divisibility of n by its lower-half divisor sum is an intrinsic, motivated relation. Ω<=3 is the complete first nontrivial multiplicative-depth classification, with two conditional quadratic prime branches and a clean prohibition for squarefree three-prime inputs; useful as a boundary for broader Ω study, not an arbitrary finite cutoff.

limitations: Claim only Ω(n)<=3; prime-output branches conditional on primality; no conclusion for Ω>=4 or infinitude.
